## Details

### elekloader

Mod loader: user supplies the stock OS file, the tool builds the custom .syx locally. Device table in the README (3016dca, 2026-11-08): Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1/Keys supported; Digitakt II 1.17 and Digitone II 1.12 experimental; Octatrack 1.40C supported (linkable core boots on an MKII); Model:Cycles and Model:Samples 1.13 supported (builds work on both units); Analog Rytm MKII 1.74 supported; Analog Four MKII 1.56 experimental proof of concept (hook bus, mod storage, unused DDR and recovery checked on a unit). Canonical repo is unclear: the forum post also embeds github.com/elekloader/elekloader (web app at elekloader.github.io/elekloader); forks exist (AvroraPolnareff, naturarum, toonst, simonjohansson); none is listed, as none has changes of its own. Forum: builder issue reported 2026-10-19. Licence GPL-2.0-or-later. 2026-11-10 (8daa2ea): the shop's list, forms and bots moved to elekloader/shop (#338); mods are submitted there. machine-pages 1.8-1.10, machines-dn1 0.5/0.6 and machines-dn2 0.5 add mono machines and MIDI CCs (emulator-tested per TESTS.md). The linker now refuses odd jump targets into mod RAM after a Digitakt II froze at boot (I61). The README offers a Windows .exe; not every release carries the macOS .dmg. 2026-11-10 (main): core-ar2 0.13 opens the Rytm MKII's TEST slots 44-52 to mod machines, adds per-voice trig and velocity getters, screen calls through stock's routines and per-mod knob ids; machine-pages 1.7 tagged. 2026-11-12 (main): core-a4mk2 0.6 brings core-ar2 0.10-0.13's foundations to the Analog Four MKII (field defaults, the modified mark, the project-save event, payloads, knob looks, screen calls) and a 37.7 MB mods' area. Builds pick older core or helper versions by themselves when a mod patches a place a newer one took (Tone+FX's Digitakt files and Digi EQ 1.0c link with DT1 core 4.0 only; OB-1 0.6 with machine-pages 1.2), and released versions stay available while a listed mod needs them. 2026-11-13 (main): a third file family, ELE2, for the Analog Rytm MKI OS 1.74 (Modwerk's Rytm MKI research holds the measurements behind the profile); the README's table also names 1.73, the profile only 1.74. core-ot 0.9-0.40 opens about 40 more Octatrack events and tables to mods (mutes, sequencer moments, LFO waves, popup rows, PATTERN SETTINGS and PERSONALIZE rows, the playback increment, card file calls, the engine task's jobs, a block to DSP core 1). 2026-11-15 (FORMAT, SDK, CORES): std1 'standard events': a mod that sets events std1 subscribes to device- neutral event names, each core maps them to its own tables, and a subscription the core does not map is refused at link time; std1 and native mods link in one build. core-a4mk2 0.7 is the first core with it and adds native A4 events for knob turns, the analog voice frame and modulation edits. A frame-check build that copied one voice's analog frame words over another's silenced track 1 and was fixed in 0.3 (unit or emulator not stated). 2026-11-16 (docs/CORES.md, DRIVE.md, FORMAT.md, core-dn1 README): on the Digitone mk1 the build descriptor now carries the stock bytes of each flashed range (ABI 1.2), and TELOS's linker refuses a +Drive mod site that is not stock on the unit, overlaps the flashed build or another mod, or a region outside a free area (link codes 21-28). core-dn1 5.4's core_stock_info copies the OS image to 0x44200000 before the OS runs. 2026-11-17 (ADAPTING, FORMAT, core-ot, settings-ot, dspload-ot, core-a4mk2 READMEs): core-ot 0.41/0.42 add 16 Octatrack events (tempo, scenes, card mount and USB DISK MODE, previews, recorder commands, pages, track select, windows, crossfader, pattern select and edits, arrangement); new dspload-ot 0.2 sends DSP code at run time (mod.json `dsp_load`), also for TELOS card mods; refusal code 23 `early` for a site the OS ran before the +Drive or card link. On the Analog Four MKII the lock service is now checked on a unit. 2026-11-18 (v0.11.0, docs/DRIVE.md, CORES.md, drive-loader-a4mk2 and drive-loader-ar2 READMEs): v0.11.0 ships the newest core of every device, core-a4mk2 0.9 included. The Analog Four MKII gets its own +Drive mods loader (drive-loader-a4mk2 0.1, not yet run): stock 1.56 keeps the +Drive as raw sectors with no file system, so the loader keeps its own two-copy store in sectors stock never addresses. The Rytm loader (0.6) now reads each file into the +Drive area itself (a 64 KB floor replaces the 512 KB staging buffer), and +Drive mods may hold storage fields, sites over the OS, claims, tables of their own, knob ids and std1 subscriptions where the build's descriptor flags allow (descriptor ABI 1.3). drive-loader-ar2's README asks for core-ar2 0.14 while core-ar2's mod.json at the tag reads 0.13. New A4 MKII check mods for live recording, the sequencer and moments (read as expected in the emulator, 2026-11-14). 2026-11-20 (ADAPTING, CORES, DRIVE, FORMAT; core-ar2 README and SKIPS.md; core-dt2, core-dn2, core-a4mk2, drive-loader, smpl-machines READMEs; new AR2 and DT2 examples): core-dt2 1.1 keeps mods' project and kit data in bytes stock writes as zeros (191 bytes a kit), adds value rows, a per-frame parameter event and key LEDs; core-dt2 1.2 and core-dn2 0.5 add what TELOS needs on the unit (card ready, project save and load, crash, restart, task list), checked in digikit's emulator only, not yet on a unit. core-ar2 0.15: knob faces, mod folders in the +Drive sample browser, pad strikes before stock and LED colours, a held USB input gain step, note ends, track mutes, DIN MIDI out, machines given slots by count; 0.16: four optional CPU skips, off at boot (silent voices, idle sample layer, the UI's dynamic_cast, idle delay and reverb), two of which change the sound slightly, and GLOBAL submenus. The linker hands out machine slots, page ids and mod-declared id pools by count, kept in the lockfile. New smpl-machines (a SMPL page machine layer) and smpl-knob-c. Five new Rytm check examples and kit-memo-dt2. core-a4mk2 0.10's core_project_keep lets the A4 loader's APPLY & RESTART keep unsaved project changes. core-a4mk2's README now says core 0.2's pages drew identically on a unit (OS 1.56). 2026-11-22 (AGENTS, ADAPTING, CORES, DRIVE; core-ar2, drive-loader-ar2 and drive-loader-a4mk2 READMEs and PAGE.md; five new Rytm check examples): core-ar2 0.17 brings the std1 standard events to the Analog Rytm MKII and adds knob flags: a mod's own knob can open a destination list as LFO DEST does (only the list bit is honoured). core-ar2 0.18 adds restart calls. drive-loader-ar2 now needs core-ar2 0.18, marks mods with saved data with * and has APPLY & RESTART, as the A4 loader. The new Rytm check examples (std, std-midi, ui, voice, knob-flags) are built and linked only. The core-ar2 README restates its OS-upgrade restart check: analog-emu hung on 5 of 15 upgrades without core's restart routine and 0 of 15 with it (0 of 30 with the panel link paced as on a unit). 2026-11-24 (docs/DRIVE.md, drive-loader READMEs): drive-loader-ar2 0.12 and drive-loader-a4mk2 0.2 give mods a versioned +Drive payload API (drive_payload_abi, count, at, find, info with id, length and sha256, dl_payload_read; imported weakly by sidecar-core) and lock a loaded mod's file until the next boot: an upload over it is kept as <name>.new and swapped in at the next boot with the new CRC written first, so a power cut cannot leave the new file under the old CRC; the MODS page shows UPDATE or LOST and refuses DELETE (IN USE: RESTART FIRST). On the A4 reads that span a card sector go straight into the caller's buffer (a 4 KB read takes 7-10 card reads, not 64-80). 2026-11-25: core-ar2 0.20 adds `ev_store_adopt` (a sound or kit saved with another layout or before core storage is handed to its mod once as it loads; example adopt-check-ar2) and mod storage fields can be pinned to fixed bits with `offset`. core-ar2 0.21 moves the Rytm MKII mods area to 0x47B48000-0x47FFF000 (4.7 MB), above stock 1.74 USB audio feedback ring at 0x47B47440-0x47B47480, which stock rewrites while a host has the audio alternate setting selected; 0.11-0.20 started at 0x47B10000 and reached that ring once a build passed 221 KB. 2026-11-26 (docs/ADAPTING.md, DRIVE.md, core-ar2 README and SKIPS.md, examples/drive-machine-check-ar2): core-ar2 0.22 lets +Drive mods add machines too: `core_machines` now spans all 19 hidden slots 34-52 (was 10, slots 34-43), and the Drive Loader's entries reach the machine table after `ev_boot_drive`, after which the project loads again (with 0.21 they never reached it). New example drive-machine-check-ar2 tests this without a +Drive.

### 1-Bit Editor

Repo was offline from 2026-11-07 (taken offline by its author with the account's other public repos, check_updates 2026-11-08) and is public again on 2026-11-19 (check_updates BACK ONLINE; README read 2026-11-19). A pixel editor for 1-bit icons and sprites in Model:Cycles and Model:Samples mods: one HTML file that runs in the browser. Canvas up to the 128 x 64 screen, drawing tools, text layers in the OS's styles, layers and groups, OS-style stamps, layout grid, guides, slices that export as separate sprites, and frames for knob-driven or timed animations. Exports a .bin in the OS's own sprite layout (y counted from the bottom, bit 7 of byte 0 is the bottom-left pixel) with a .json describing the screen for a mod author or an agent, plus PNGs. Licence: MIT. Listed by altstrument.

_Sources: altstrument (2026-11-01), README, CHANGELOG (2026-11-19)_

### Modded Cycles

One community OS for Model:Cycles 1.13, built in a browser from your own files (needs a Syntakt 1.41/1.42 file for its engines): sampler, Syntakt engines, Braids and Open303 machines, extra LFOs, arp, 6-ch USB audio. Experimental on Model:Samples. Licence: MIT; distribution: browser-installer. Listed by altstrument; repo not read by us yet.

_Related: cites `elektron-firmware-tool` (README credits); cites `elektroid` (README credits: the Elektron Transfer update protocol behind fast USB flashing); bundles `model-tg` (README: Model-TG's Sampler as the 7th machine); bundles `elektron-model-tweaks` (README: includes drumkilla's tweaks (latching mute, trig preview)); bundles `ms-multi-output` (README: 6-channel audio after scottmetoyer/ms-multi-output); cites `octamax` (README credits: reverse-engineering method); cites `octa-bt-pt` (README credits: reverse-engineering and patching) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: altstrument (2026-11-01), README (2026-11-11)_

_Related: builds on `modded-cycles` (README: built on Modded-Cycles and Model-TG); builds on `model-tg` (README: Model-TG is ticked with model909) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### ElekPrep (elektron-sample-prep)

Single-page browser sample prep: trims at zero crossings, converts to 48 kHz 16-bit WAV, works out loop lengths from BPM and steps; profiles for four devices (device list taken from the related ElekPrep Transfer app, not checked). No MIDI; files go to the unit through Transfer or Elektroid. MIT.

_Sources: altstrument (2026-11-03), README_

### ElekPrep Transfer

Closed-source browser app that preps audio and sends it over Web MIDI SysEx to the +Drive, with Transfer and +Drive Manager views and device profiles for Digitakt II, Digitakt, Analog Rytm (MKI/MKII) and Model:Samples. Proprietary; author not named. Relation to luizvarela's ElekPrep not established (same name). Interesting as a second independent implementation of +Drive upload over SysEx.

_Sources: altstrument (2026-11-03)_

### Elektron Model:Samples mods (Yan Hugman)

Six .elemod files picked in the Elekloader shop for the Model:Samples; the build is sent as an OS update. Only the main OS is changed; recovery is the stock OS 1.13 .syx over 5-pin MIDI from the startup menu (FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4). LOCKS counter brings its own layout of the right side of the main screen and should not be combined with other mods that change that area. LOCKS duplicate fix works around a stock bug (SB41). Builds on drumkilla's elektron-model-tweaks. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-25.

_Related: mod for `elekloader` (README: add the .elemod files in Elekloader for Model:Samples; core is added automatically); builds on `elektron-model-tweaks` (README credits: the mods build on drumkilla's elektron-model-tweaks) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: state/NEW.md 2026-11-25, README, LICENSE, file list (2026-11-25)_

### Modded Cycles Techno Edition

25 machines (Elektron's six plus 19: 909/808/606 voices, rumble kick, modal metal, additive drum, acid and growl basses, Braids, VA, cross-mod, 6-op FM, pad, and a sampler / granular / wavetable engine), a filter and insert effect per track, sidechain, master DJ EQ, 6-channel USB audio, CPU monitor and budget; plus a VST3/AU/standalone plug-in that follows the Cycles and reads sounds back. Built locally from the official OS (Python only), checked byte for byte. README: every part tested in emulation, and played on real hardware. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-05. 2026-11-14: the repo moved from mbreilly/Modded_f-king_cycles to mbreilly/Modded_cycles_techno_edition (same history; the old URL redirects). 2026-11-16 (README, CHANGELOG, docs/MACHINES.md): 26 machines; the author takes bug reports but no feature requests and invites forks. The web builder uses a JavaScript port of drumkilla's mtlib. 2026-11-17 (README, CHANGELOG v1.2/v1.3): the builders take an optional DX7 bank for the DX machine (algorithm, feedback, operator ratios, levels, envelopes and velocity are used; keyboard scaling, pitch envelope, LFO and AM are not), and the built-in sounds ship as a DX7 bank for Dexed. v1.3 fixes four machine bugs, among them a RUMBL tail that could hum on and keep using CPU. The repo no longer holds any bytes of Elektron's firmware: each patch checks the original bytes by length and SHA-256. 2026-11-18 (CHANGELOG v1.4-v1.6, README, MACHINES.md): 27 machines with UBSAW (seven detuned saws on the curves of a published JP-8000 analysis, written from scratch); an Attack stage after the filter and insert effect on all 27 machines; the CPU budget's default raised to 80 % because a project made before flashing already counts about 74 % with the six stock machines (I140). The README now documents what happens to projects moved between this firmware, the official OS and other mods, and a clean switching procedure. 2026-11-19 (README, CHANGELOG v1.6.1-v1.6.2): the web builder and patch.py --machine samples take both official OS 1.13 files (Cycles and Samples) and pack this firmware inside the Samples OS, as Modded-Cycles does, so bootloader, startup menu and signature stay Elektron's; the result turns a Model:Samples into a modded Model:Cycles. Installed through the startup menu (FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4) over MIDI IN; after that Transfer can no longer update it. Going back: the official Samples OS through the startup menu, after setting tracks on added machines back to stock machines. A Model:Cycles running the Samples OS would accept the file and then refuse Cycles firmware over USB until the Cycles OS is reinstalled over MIDI. 2026-11-20 (README, CHANGELOG v1.6.3-v1.9, MACHINES.md): 28 machines with 707 (machine 28, after UBSAW so project machine numbers stay; six synthesised parts at 24 kHz and 8 bits, cymbals 6 bits). Trig preview (hold a trig, press PAGE while stopped) taken from drumkilla's mod. Turing Machine LFO waves T3-T16 (a looping random sequence of 3 to 16 steps; a stock OS reads them as RND). UBSAW lost its own filter and Attack in v1.6.5, so its projects from v1.5-v1.6.4 sound different. v1.9: the Cycles' mute only holds back sequencer trigs, so ATMOS's trigless GATE drone kept sounding on a muted track; it now stops on mute (user report). 2026-11-23 (CHANGELOG v1.10, README): v1.10 turns the retrig into an arpeggiator on every track (FUNC + RETRIG: Arp, Oct, Chd with 12 chord types, Gat, Lat); a retrig on a trig arpeggiates that note and its chord at the retrig rate, or RETRIG held plays it live. The live arpeggiator comes from the original Modded Cycles; chords, sequencer use, gate and latch are new. Tested in emulation, not yet on hardware. 2026-11-24 (CHANGELOG v1.10.1, v1.11): LFO 2 on every track (FADE, Sph, MODE and Pol shared with LFO 1; both on one destination add up), an LFO 2 page in the plug-in; PUNCH now acts on the machines that use the Cycles' own amp envelope (projects saved with PUNCH on them sound punchier); the manual is at its eighteenth edition (56 pages). Tested in emulation, not yet on hardware. 2026-11-25: v1.12: SLR tested in the emulator only and the new plug-in look built and tested on Linux; neither played on hardware yet (CHANGELOG).

### Model:Samples battery base

Open-hardware battery base using the original side mounting points and the left battery input: editable CAD, STEP/STL, parts list, build guide and printable fit gauges. No working physical prototype validated yet. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-07.

_Sources: GitHub search 2026-11-07, README, README (2026-11-11)_

### ms-vis (Model:Samples visualizer)

An audio-reactive visualizer in one HTML page (Three.js and Web MIDI) that follows the Model:Samples' notes, CCs, clock and program changes; presets, projector mode and video recording. Nothing is sent to the device. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-16. 2026-11-18 (README): out of the box a Model:Samples sent only the MIDI clock over USB in the author's tests; the visualizer needs CLK OUT and PCH OUT on, OUT TO = M+U and FILTER > ENCS = I+E in the CONFIG menu. 2026-11-22 (README): a Snare flash slider sets or turns off the snare's picture inversion (for photosensitive viewers), and checkboxes choose which MIDI channels' encoder CCs move the visuals, because the Model:Samples sends encoder turns on the selected track's channel. Nothing new on the device side.

_Sources: state/NEW.md 2026-11-16, README (2026-11-16), README (2026-11-18), README (2026-11-22)_
